## KB Compaction & Consolidation (Future Infrastructure)

> **Added:** 2026-02-09 | **Type:** 🛠️ Infrastructure | **Status:** HIGH PRIORITY (escalated 2026-02-09)
> **Why:** 24,000+ articles → most token cost comes from searching noise. Compaction = faster retrieval, cheaper sessions, better signal.
> **User directive:** "Don't just add knowledge — extract insights and learnings. Process into knowledge graph. Make sure there's no fluff or slop. Better Obsidian utilization for traversal."
> **When:** After Wave 2-3 scraping completes (imminent). Before any new scraping waves.

### Phase 1: Quick Wins (Dedup & Prune)
- Remove exact/near-duplicate articles across sources (MFCC-style dedup for text)
- Prune stub articles (<100 chars of real content)
- Remove boilerplate (nav, footer, sidebar) that wasn't stripped during scrape
- **Strip filler text** — cookie notices, newsletter CTAs, social share blocks, repeated navigation, ad placeholders, "subscribe to our newsletter" blocks. Reduce noise so advisors get signal only.
- **Prompt injection prevention** — Sanitize all scraped content before KB ingestion. Strip phrases like "ignore previous instructions", "you are now", "system:", hidden HTML/CSS text, zero-width characters, and encoded payloads. Build into scraping pipeline as a pre-processing step (runs before article is written to disk).
- Estimated savings: 10-20% of total article volume

### Phase 2: Index Layer (Structured Navigation)
- Build per-advisor topic indexes (like Lenny's `index/` dir) for all advisors
- TF-IDF or embedding-based clustering to group articles by topic
- Generate summary cards per cluster (title, key insight, article refs)
- Result: Claude reads index first (small), then pulls specific articles (targeted)

### Phase 3: Semantic Compression
- Summarize long articles into structured abstracts (key points, code snippets, quotes)
